name: SGLang (observability surface: Prometheus metrics + OpenTelemetry with per-stage slices)
notable_features: Metrics require an explicit `--enable-metrics`; nothing is exposed at /metrics without it

All core latency metrics exist with the same names as vLLM: `sglang:time_to_first_token_seconds`, `sglang:inter_token_latency_seconds`, `sglang:request_time_per_output_token_seconds`, `sglang:e2e_request_latency_seconds`, `sglang:queue_time_seconds`

TTFT and TPOT carry an `is_streaming` label (the source comments this exists because 'stream' is a reserved thrift keyword so downstream schema columns cannot carry it), which lets you separate streaming from non-streaming latency - vLLM has no such split

The richest KV-cache instrumentation of any engine: not one utilization gauge but a documented pool decomposition - `sglang:token_usage` (max across full/swa/mamba pools), `sglang:full_token_usage`, `sglang:swa_token_usage`, `sglang:mamba_usage`, plus absolute counts `sglang:kv_available_tokens`, `sglang:kv_evictable_tokens`, `sglang:kv_used_tokens` with the stated invariant kv_available + kv_evictable + kv_used <= max_total_num_tokens

Retraction (SGLang's word for preemption) is directly measured: `sglang:num_retracted_reqs` (Gauge), `sglang:num_retracted_requests_total`, `sglang:num_retracted_input_tokens_total`, `sglang:num_retracted_output_tokens_total` - the input/output token split tells you whether the recompute cost is prompt-side or decode-side
A per-stage latency histogram `sglang:per_stage_req_latency_seconds{stage=...}` fed by the same RequestStage enum that names the trace slices, so metrics and traces use one vocabulary

OTel tracing with `--enable-trace` + `--otlp-traces-endpoint`, a runtime-adjustable level 0-3 (GET /set_trace_level, no restart), and `SGLANG_TRACE_ASYNC=1` which moves span creation off the hot path into a ZMQ exporter process because synchronous span creation measurably degrades throughput under large batch
hardware_caveats: OpenTelemetry is NOT bundled: process_tracing_init() raises RuntimeError('opentelemetry package is not installed!!!') unless opentelemetry-sdk/api/exporter-otlp/exporter-otlp-proto-grpc are installed. The extra is `pip install -e "python[tracing]"`
Only two OTLP protocols are accepted, grpc (default) and http/protobuf; anything else raises ValueError

`sglang:utilization` and `sglang:max_running_requests_under_SLO` are documented-but-dead on current main. The metrics reporter carries the comment 'TODO: max_running_requests_under_SLO has no setter - sglang:utilization stuck at 0 (regressed #22713)' and the scheduler passes max_running_requests_under_SLO=None with 'TODO: ... dead chain'. Do not build an autoscaling rule on them
Under `--disaggregation-mode prefill` the reporter sets utilization = -1, so an alert reading 'utilization above 1' is not a bug on a prefill worker
With TP > 1 only TP rank 0 records request metrics unless `--enable-metrics-for-all-schedulers` is set; otherwise all metrics appear to come from TP 0, which matters under dp_attention
best_for: Reading a disaggregated prefill/decode deployment: `sglang:kv_transfer_speed_gb_s`, `sglang:kv_transfer_latency_ms`, `sglang:kv_transfer_bootstrap_ms`, `sglang:kv_transfer_alloc_ms`, `sglang:kv_transfer_total_mb`, and per-stage gauges for prealloc/bootstrap/wait/transfer/host-receive queues make the handoff itself observable, and a CI test asserts the matching trace spans exist

Diagnosing decode-memory pressure: retracted-request counters plus `sglang:num_used_tokens` and the available/evictable/used split identify whether the cache is full because of long prompts or too many concurrent decodes
Hybrid-attention or SSM models, where the swa_token_usage / mamba_usage gauges are the only way to see per-pool pressure
avoid_for: Forgetting `--enable-metrics` and concluding the engine has no metrics - it does, they are just off by default
Tracing at full level on a large-batch server without SGLANG_TRACE_ASYNC=1

Assuming the ITL histogram and per-request TPOT histogram are interchangeable; the ITL observer divides each wall-clock interval by num_new_tokens and increments the bucket num_new_tokens times, so the two carry different weights by construction
notes: Metric names transcribed from SGLangMetricsCollector in python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py on main (~180 name= occurrences, most conditional on feature flags). Core set: `sglang:num_running_reqs`, `sglang:num_queue_reqs`, `sglang:gen_throughput` ('The generation throughput (token/s)'), `sglang:cache_hit_rate`, `sglang:decode_sum_seq_lens`, `sglang:token_usage`, `sglang:full_token_usage`, `sglang:swa_token_usage`, `sglang:mamba_usage`, `sglang:num_used_tokens`, `sglang:kv_available_tokens`, `sglang:kv_evictable_tokens`, `sglang:kv_used_tokens`, `sglang:prompt_tokens_total`, `sglang:generation_tokens_total`, `sglang:cached_tokens_total`, `sglang:num_requests_total`, `sglang:num_aborted_requests_total`, `sglang:time_to_first_token_seconds` (label is_streaming), `sglang:inter_token_latency_seconds`, `sglang:request_time_per_output_token_seconds` (label is_streaming, documented as (finished_time - first_token_time) / (completion_tokens - 1)), `sglang:e2e_request_latency_seconds` (label is_streaming), `sglang:queue_time_seconds`, `sglang:per_stage_req_latency_seconds` (label stage), `sglang:uncached_prompt_tokens_histogram`, `sglang:prompt_tokens_histogram`, `sglang:generation_tokens_histogram`, `sglang:utilization`, `sglang:new_token_ratio`, `sglang:is_cuda_graph`, `sglang:max_total_num_tokens`, `sglang:kv_cache_memory_usage_gb`, `sglang:weight_memory_usage_gb`, `sglang:graph_memory_usage_gb{phase}`, `sglang:startup_time_seconds`, `sglang:page_size`, `sglang:num_pages`, `sglang:context_len`, `sglang:max_running_requests_under_SLO` (dead). The source itself flags `sglang:token_usage` as 'FIXME: misleadingly named' since it is the max across pools. Speculative decoding: `sglang:spec_accept_length`, `sglang:spec_accept_rate`, `sglang:spec_num_steps`, `sglang:spec_num_draft_tokens`, `sglang:spec_block_accept_length`. Also present and useful: `sglang:scheduler_idle_seconds_total`, `sglang:forward_execution_seconds_total`, `sglang:scheduler_stage_seconds_total`, `sglang:estimated_flops_per_gpu_total`, `sglang:estimated_read_bytes_per_gpu_total`. Trace shape: a root span named f'{role} Req {rid[:8]}' (role empty when unified, 'prefill'/'decode' otherwise) with attributes rid and module=sglang::{module_name}, plus bootstrap_room when set, over the incoming traceparent; then per-thread and per-slice spans named by RequestStage.stage_name at level 1-4. Stage names verbatim: tokenize, api_server_dispatch, dpc_dispatch, request_process, prefill_waiting, decode_forward, decode_loop, prefill_forward, chunked_prefill, mm_encode, prefill_prepare, prefill_bootstrap, prefill_transfer_kv_cache, decode_prepare, decode_bootstrap, decode_waiting, decode_transferred, fake_output, quick_finish, spec_draft, spec_verify, run_batch_cpu; mooncake adds mooncake_send, mooncake_recv, mooncake_worker_send, mooncake_worker_send_session, mooncake_worker_recv. TTFT definition from the docs is precise and worth quoting: 'time from request creation in the API server to the first token. For streaming requests it ends when the first output arrives after detokenization, which may contain no printable text' - so a detokenizer stall lands in TTFT. Retraction mechanics: when check_decode_mem() fails the scheduler logs 'KV cache pool is full. Retract requests. #retracted_reqs: N, #new_tokens_gained: M', calls release_kv_cache(is_insert=False) so the freed KV does not go back into the radix tree, and requeues; requests with no host backup are aborted with HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE rather than silently recomputed.
